c.tagline: Sicily's sun-baked capital, where Arab-Norman splendour meets raucous street-food markets.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are white and metered, though a fixed fare of around €45 applies from the airport to the centre. Uber offers only its licensed taxi/black-car service in Palermo (no UberX), so hailing at a rank or booking through Free Now or the itTaxi/appTaxi apps is the norm; agree the fare before longer rides.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 113 reaches state police and 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing/scooter bag-snatching in the markets (Ballarò, Vucciria); caution at night

hood_desc: The dense historic core around the Quattro Canti, the Cathedral, and the Ballaro market, where Arab-Norman monuments, baroque churches, and street-food stalls sit side by side; best for first-timers who want the sights and the buzz within walking distance.

A once-faded seaside quarter reborn as Palermo's arty heart, with the Foro Italico promenade, Palazzo Abatellis, lively piazzas, and a wave of galleries, cafes, and craft-cocktail bars; suits travellers after character and an evening scene.

Home to the atmospheric Vucciria market, sleepy by day and rowdy by night when its squares fill with students, street food, and open-air drinking; good for travellers who want to be in the thick of the nightlife.

The elegant modern centre around Teatro Politeama and the boutique-lined Via della Liberta, with grand 19th-century buildings, upscale shops, and reliable restaurants; suits those wanting a smarter, calmer base with easy transport.

Palermo's belle-epoque seaside resort about 20 minutes from the centre, with a crescent of white sand, art-nouveau villas, and seafood restaurants beneath Monte Pellegrino; ideal for a relaxed, beachy stay.

water.note: Tap water is officially safe, though most locals drink bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Buses and the four tram lines run roughly 5:30 AM to around midnight; a limited night bus network and taxis cover the late-night hours.
transit.note: AMAT runs the city buses and four modern tram lines (opened 2015), while Trenitalia's suburban 'passante ferroviario' rail links the main stations and the airport; buses remain the backbone for reaching most sights in the historic centre.
transit.pay: A single AMAT ticket is €1.40 and valid 90 minutes across buses and trams; a day pass is €3.50. Tickets are sold at tobacconists, newsstands, and machines, and contactless tap-and-go is being rolled out. Validate on board to avoid fines.

bus: Palermo Centrale / Piazzale Cairoli coach stops (Flixbus & intercity)

transit.m: Trinacria Express train to Palermo Centrale (~50 min, ~2/hour)
Prestia e Comande bus to city centre (~50 min, hourly)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a cover charge (coperto) is usually on the bill, so rounding up or leaving a euro or two for good service is appreciated but not expected.
